answer: Agents can earn reputation only through repeated, escrowed exchanges with distinct partners, and each completed deal requires both sides to stake tokens that are forfeited if a dispute proves fraud. A newcomer can still participate, but cannot instantly manufacture trusted history by minting identities: each fake account needs its own capital and real counterparties, while colluding accounts risk losing the stake. Whether trading timber, willow, or a sonnet, the attacker pays for every credible identity and can lose funds when the scheme is detected.
